chung.Syllabus Name: Kỹ năng vận hành dịch vụ ẩm thực
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description:
- Main objective: This course aims to equip students with practical operational skills to plan, implement and supervise food and beverage services, manage key resources, and apply standard operating procedures to deliver safe, efficient and guest‑oriented F&B operations in hospitality settings.

- Description: This course examines the managerial and supervisory functions within F&B departments, including menu and service concepts, basic production and service workflows, cost and inventory control, quality, safety and hygiene, and the coordination of front‑ and back‑of‑house activities to meet financial, managerial and guest satisfaction objectives. Students are also expected to utilize contemporary AI tools (namely Gemini, ChatGPT or Copilot) to support industry research, scenario analysis, and the development of concept visuality or practical tasks in a responsible and ethical manner.

-Teaching method: Through lecture, hands-on practice, roleplay, case studies, and simulated operational scenarios.

- Facility and equipment requirement : Depending on the training condition of each campus, the course will be implemented in school lab designed up to 4-5* hotel standard, real hotel or other places, which fully met with requirements.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Students are required to attend with professional grooming standards.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time.

- Students are encouraged to use laptop in class only for learning purpose as well as comply with the time and regulation.

taiLieu: John Cousins, Dennis Lillicrap, Suzanne Weekes
clo: Explain key sectors, structures, functions, and stages of food and beverage operations, and outline key factors of meal experience and customer service.
Demonstrate professional attributes, technical skills, service conventions, and interpersonal behaviours, including teamwork, discipline, and communication in F&B settings.
Apply health, safety, and security protocols, and optimize service areas, serviceware for efficient F&B operations.
Describe food production and service methods, demonstrate knowledge of foods, beverages, menu types, basic menu development, and key characteristics of different service styles.
Execute standard operating procedures for different service styles and events, following appropriate service sequences in front‑ and back‑of‑house operations.
Apply basic F&B supervisory knowledge in legal control, sales, pricing, staffing, and performance measures to support operational and financial objectives.
